# Data Quality Report

**Dataset:** `Consumer_Complaints.xlsx`
**Scope:** Data Analytics track, AnalystLab Africa Week 4
**Evidence:** every figure is generated by the scripts in `python_files/` (`data_inspection.py`, `data_cleaning.py`, `validation.py`). Run `python run_pipeline.py` to regenerate the full raw profile.

## Contents
1. Overall assessment
2. Raw data profile
3. Issue log
4. Interpretation rules
5. Cleaning
6. Validation results
7. Questions the data cannot answer

## Overall Assessment
The dataset is **fit for analysis**. It is complete and internally consistent, with no duplicate keys, invalid dates or gaps in time. Every blank value has an explainable meaning. No records needed to be removed or corrected. The cleaning work is about **labelling, deriving fields and flagging**, not repairing.

| Dimension | Result | Rating |
|---|---|---|
| Completeness | 62,516 rows × 12 columns, matching the brief. 76 of 76 months present | High |
| Uniqueness | 62,516 distinct Complaint IDs, 0 duplicate rows | High |
| Validity | All dates parse. 51 valid state codes. No whitespace or case variants | High |
| Consistency | Forwarding interval never negative. Timely blanks match In progress exactly | High |
| Timeliness / coverage | Aug 2023 partial month. 2017 (May–Dec) and 2023 (Jan–Aug) partial years | Flagged |
| Possible repeat submissions | 248 rows in 120 same-attribute groups with near-consecutive IDs | Flagged, kept |

## Issue log
| # | Field(s) | Finding | Count | Interpretation | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DQ1 | Timely response? | Blank values | 1,494 (2.39%) | Every blank is a complaint marked *In progress* (submitted 12 May – 28 Aug 2023). The response is pending, not untimely. | New column `Timely Response Status` = Yes / No / **Pending**. Pending is **excluded from the timely % denominator** and reported separately (brief §5-B). |
| DQ2 | Sub-issue | Blank values | 10,858 (17.37%) | Per the data dictionary, not every issue has sub-issues. Concentrated in Mortgage (6,362) and all Money transfer records (3,453). | Labelled "No sub-issue recorded". Not counted as a defect. |
| DQ3 | Company public response | Blank values | 2,175 (3.48%) | The public response is optional for the company. 1,550 of the blanks are from 2023, which fits responses not yet posted for recent complaints. | Labelled "No public response recorded". Kept separate from the 60,311 "chose not to respond publicly". |
| DQ4 | Sub-product | Blank values | 7 (0.01%) | All are *Checking or savings account* records with credit-reporting issues. | Labelled "Not provided". Flagged `DQ Missing Sub-product`. |
| DQ5 | All non-ID fields | Same-attribute groups | 2,784 rows in 1,290 groups | Distinct IDs, so distinct complaints per the brief. In 120 groups (248 rows) the IDs are within 5 of each other, a possible repeat submission. | **Kept.** Flagged `DQ Same-Attribute Group` and `DQ Possible Repeat Submission` for sensitivity checks. |
| DQ6 | Date submitted | Partial reporting periods | Aug 2023 (to 28th). 2017 = May–Dec. 2023 = Jan–Aug | A month and year-over-year comparison involving 2023 understates the full year. | Flags `Is Partial Month`, `Is Partial Year`. Visuals and YoY must label 2023 as partial. |
| DQ7 | Date submitted | First month | May 2017 starts on the 1st | May itself is complete within the extract, but **2017 is a partial year** (8 of 12 months). | 2017 is flagged as a partial year. Annual comparisons use full years (2018–2022) or the same Jan–Aug window. |
| DQ8 | Company response to consumer | "Closed" with no detail | 8 | Older generic category. All 8 have Timely = No. | Kept as its own category. |
| DQ9 | Forwarding interval | Long tail | Max 275 days. 435 records > 30 days | Median is 0 days, so most complaints are forwarded the same day. A small number take far longer. | Flag `Is Long Forwarding Interval` (> 30 days ≈ 99.3rd percentile). Bands for distribution visuals. |
| DQ10 | Issue × Product | Same issue under several products | 13 issues | Credit-reporting issues are filed against card, mortgage and bank products. This is how the CFPB form works. | No change. Explained in the documentation. |

## Interpretation Rules Applied
1. *Complaint ID* is the primary key. It was verified unique.
2. *Date submitted* is when the CFPB *received* the complaint. *Date received* is when the CFPB *sent it to the company*.
3. (Date received − Date submitted) is the *CFPB forwarding interval*. It is never presented as company response or resolution time.
4. Blank timely response is never treated as "No".
5. A complaint is a consumer-reported issue, not evidence of misconduct. Company response categories are recorded classifications, not proof of satisfactory resolution.

## Cleaning
Script: `python_files/data_cleaning.py`
Input: `Consumer_Complaints.xlsx` (read only)
Output: `cleaned_dataset.csv`
Result: 62,516 rows in → 62,516 rows out. 12 original columns kept as they were, plus 22 derived or labelled columns (34 total).

### Principles
- Raw file is never modified. The pipeline reads it and writes a new file.
- No rows removed. There were no duplicate keys or duplicate rows, and there is no basis for exclusion.
- Original values preserved. Each cleaned value goes in a new column, so any figure can be traced back to the source.
- Fully reproducible. Rerunning the script produces the same output, and `src/validation.py` checks it (23 checks, all passing).

### Transformation Log

| Step | Column(s) created | Rule | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | (originals) | Dates normalised to day precision. Leading and trailing whitespace stripped from text (none found) | Type safety |
| 2 | `Year`, `Quarter`, `Year Quarter`, `Month Number`, `Month Name`, `Year Month` | From Date submitted. `Year Month` = first day of the month | Year, month and quarter fields |
| 3 | `Is Partial Month`, `Is Partial Year` | Partial month = Aug 2023. Partial year = 2017 (May–Dec) and 2023 (Jan–Aug) | DQ6: avoid misleading trend and YoY comparisons |
| 4 | `Forwarding Interval Days` | Date received − Date submitted, in days | This is the CFPB forwarding interval, not resolution time |
| 5 | `Forwarding Interval Band` | 0 · 1 · 2–7 · 8–30 · >30 days | Distribution visual (Page 4) |
| 6 | `Is Long Forwarding Interval` | Interval > 30 days | "Unusually long" identification (Page 4). The threshold is in `src/config.py` |
| 7 | `Product Short` | Map of 9 long CFPB product names to short labels | Readable dashboard labels. Originals kept |
| 8 | `Sub-product Clean` | Blank → "Not provided" | DQ4 |
| 9 | `Sub-issue Clean` | Blank → "No sub-issue recorded" | DQ2 |
| 10 | `Public Response Clean` | Shortened labels. Blank → "No public response recorded" | DQ3 |
| 11 | `Timely Response Status` | Yes / No kept. Blank → "Pending" | DQ1. Brief rule: blank ≠ No |
| 12 | `Timely Valid For KPI` | True only for Yes/No (61,022 records) | denominator definition |
| 13 | `Is In Progress` | Company response = "In progress" (1,494) | KPI 10 |
| 14 | `DQ Missing Sub-product`, `DQ Missing Public Response` | Blank flags | Traceability |
| 15 | `DQ Same-Attribute Group`, `DQ Possible Repeat Submission` | Identical on all 11 non-ID fields. Possible repeat = IDs in the group span ≤ 5 | DQ5: kept, flagged |

### Category Standardization
No case, spelling or whitespace variants were found in Product, Sub-product, Issue, Sub-issue, Submitted via or State. Standardization was therefore limited to *display labels* (steps 7 and 10) and *explicit labels for blanks* (steps 8–11). Category counts before and after match exactly (validation check "Category counts reconcile").

## Questions the Data Cannot Answer
- How long the company took to respond or resolve a complaint. The dataset has no response date.
- Whether complaints were valid, or whether consumers were satisfied. There is no dispute field.
- Complaint narratives or sentiment, which are not supplied.
- Consumer demographics beyond state, and monetary amounts of relief.
